title.narrative: Assam Integrated Flood and Riverbank Erosion Risk Management Investment Program - Project 2

description.narrative: Incorporating lessons from Project 1, Project 2 for $60.16 million will fund a combination of structural and nonstructural measures in the three subproject areas (Palasbari-Gumi, Kaziranga, and Dibrugarh) along the Brahmaputra River in Assam. The structural measures will include: (i) 20 kilometers (km) of riverbank protection works with innovative technologies, combined with 5 km of pro-siltation measures; (ii) upgrade of 13 km of flood embankments; and (iii) construction of four sluice gates and one pumping station to improve drainage. Monitoring and adaptive maintenance of the infrastructure will also be included to cope with the highly dynamic morphological processes of the river. The nonstructural measures will continue the methodologies used under Project 1 and cover community involvement and community-based flood risk management activities.

Output: Multidisciplinary investment program management strengthened. Indicator: Female representation in FREMAA staff increased to 33% Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: Status quo prevails. Data Source: FREMAA and WRD annual reports

Output: Comprehensive FRERM structural and nonstructural measures developed, implemented and maintained in three subproject areas Indicator: At least 85% of the members of 32 existing DMCs trained/retrained on flood disaster preparedness Achievement: N Progress/Status: 85% of members of 32 new DMCs trained or retrained in flood disaster preparedness. Data Source: FREMAA, WRD and ASDMA annual reports Actual value: N

Output: Comprehensive FRERM structural and nonstructural measures developed, implemented and maintained in three subproject areas Indicator: At least 43 additional DMCs (with at least 30% women representation) at district, block, gram panchayat, and highly vulnerable villages established and functional Achievement: N Progress/Status: 43 new DMCs have been established and are functional. Data Source: FREMAA, WRD and ASDMA annual reports Actual value: N

Output: Institutional and knowledge-based flood and riverbank erosion risk management (FRERM) planning strengthened Indicator: Flood and erosion management plan with gender-inclusive elements updated, finalized and endorsed by FREMAA for implementation Achievement: N Progress/Status: Flood and erosion management plan prepared in 2014 was updated with gender-inclusive elements. The last updated plan includes GIS-based assessment of riverbank erosion along the Brahmaputra River in Assam over the last two decades. The combination of socio-economic, geographic, and hydro-meteorological data allowed to identify erosion ‘hot-spots' through multi-criteria analysis and to identify priority areas. Data Source: FREMAA and WRD annual reports

Output: Institutional and knowledge-based flood and riverbank erosion risk management (FRERM) planning strengthened Indicator: Flood forecasting model and GIS-based erosion prediction model finalized Achievement: N Progress/Status: A flood forecasting model was developed using a wide variety of hydro-meteorological and geographic data to enhance the lead time of flood prediction along the main stem of the Brahmaputra. The model was tested during successive floods and improved and might become available for user agencies before monsoon 2021. A flood forecasting model was developed using a wide variety of hydro-meteorological and geographic data to enhance the lead time of flood prediction along the main stem of the Brahmaputra. The model was tested during successive floods and improved and might become available for user agencies before monsoon 2021. On erosion prediction model, an Embankment Breach Risk Assessment and Prediction Report was prepared which identified dominant failure mechanisms of the flood embankments alongside the Brahmaputra main stem and developed a scientific framework to assess the risks of breaching, as well as a Management Information System (MIS)-based breach forecasting model. Data Source: FREMAA and WRD annual reports Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Resilience to flood and riverbank erosion risks in selected flood-prone areas along the Brahmaputra River increased.

Land loss from riverbank erosion within the three subproject areas reduced by 80% (unit: hectares land loss per year) Achievement: 46 Progress/Status: EA has reported that in 115 sample villages, erosion loss has been reported only in 3 villages. Earlier, during the MTR Mission in early 2020, the assessment on land loss from riverbank erosion within the three subproject areas from 2018 to 2019 was 95 hectares, which was a reduction of 59% over the 2018 baseline of 230 hectares. Data Source: Long-term erosion statistics as part of the erosion prediction tool

42,500 ha of urban, agricultural, and other flood-prone lands with approximately 1 million people along 90 km critical reaches of the Brahmaputra River protected (unit: hectare) Achievement: 35000 Progress/Status: As reported by the EA, total area protected through various structures, was 90961 ha in the three sub project areas (45120 ha in urban area and 44971 rural area). Data Source: FREMAA and WRD annual reports

No flood damages resulting from embankment breaches along the three subproject areas incurred (unit: INR) Progress/Status: Embankment breaches have not been reported in any of the locations where structures have been completed.
